newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks end down after rallying to record high.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end down after rallying to record high.

text.p: Hong Kong share prices ended lower on Thursday after a strong morning rally into record ground was followed by profit-taking during the afternoon.
The Hang Seng Index fell 29.58 points, or 0.19 percent, to 15,709.23 after hitting an all-time high of 15,880.57 earlier.
"There was bound to be some profit-taking," said DBS Securities director of research Percy Au-Young.

The Hang Seng Index rallied 292.03 points on Wednesday and investors followed through early on Thursday, snapping up conglomerate and property stocks and spurred by overnight record highs on Wall Street.

"We are just going through a whole rotation thing at the moment. Hutchison and Swire have had the big moves and the properties are up a little bit," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading CS First Boston.
Hutchison Whampoa Ltd soared HK$1.50 to HK$70.25 and Swire Pacific Ltd advanced HK$2.25 to HK$69.25.
But utilities, which have been strong performers, succumbed to profit-taking with Hongkong Telecom falling HK$0.40 to HK$20.00 and China Light and Power down HK$0.40 at HK$44.70.
"The market is digesting its gains and volumes are dropping," said Verin.
Turnover on Thursday was HK$18.33 billion, up from Wednesday's HK$16.31 billion but down from last week's daily average of HK$21.08 billion.
Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities, said jitters in the currency market had also hurt the market.

Hong Kong dollar forward rates soared on Thursday amid rumours about speculative interest and hedging on Hong Kong dollar positions by nervous investors. "It sent a few shivers in the market because we were at an all-time high," said Remington.
Property stocks moved ahead following a good response to Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd flat sales in the New Territories.
Cheung Kong said a flat sale at its Vista Paradiso project was 50 times subscribed. The stock rose HK$0.50 to HK$75.25.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd rose HK$0.50 to HK$90.75.
Brokers said the market needed to get some good news from the property market to move significantly higher from here.
Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd fell HK$0.25 to HK$11.40 after reporting disappointing interim net profit growth of eight percent to HK$412 million.
Angang New Steel Co Ltd made its market debut and ended at HK$1.70 compared with an issue price of HK$1.63.
